verdict.rationale: Firestore is documented as a managed database with no servers to run, and client apps can read, write, listen to and query it, including offline with later sync. Server-side access is only implied: MongoDB-compatible drivers are available in the Enterprise edition, and a community user runs production APIs on Functions with Firestore as the database. Missing for 10: an explicit documented provisioning flow, first-party documentation of server/Admin SDK database read/write (beyond Enterprise MongoDB drivers), and hands-on corroboration of client-plus-server SDK usage.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision a managed database and read/write it from client and server SDKs

citations.quote: Store and sync app data at global scale without managing servers.
Cloud Firestore caches data that your app is actively using, so the app can write, read, listen to, and query data even if the device is offline.
it keeps your data in sync across client apps through realtime listeners and offers offline support for mobile and web
You can use existing MongoDB application code, drivers, tools, and the open-source ecosystem of MongoDB integrations with Cloud Firestore in the Firestore Enterprise edition.
